title: Present tense, -ir verbs
goal: By the end of this lesson you can conjugate regular -ir verbs like finir and choisir in the present, use the -iss- plural forms correctly, and understand how they are shortened in Quebec speech.

body: Regular -ir verbs (the second group) drop *-ir* and add *-is, -is, -it, -issons, -issez, -issent*. The key is the *-iss-* that appears in the plural.
In speech, *je finis*, *tu finis* and *il finit* all sound the same [fi-ni]. The plural is where you hear the difference: *ils finissent* [fi-niss].
learn.tip: Singular: s, s, t. Plural: add -iss- before the normal endings.

body: Many of these verbs describe a change or a result: *grandir* (to grow up), *vieillir* (to get older), *maigrir* (to lose weight), *grossir* (to gain weight), *rougir* (to blush).
Others are everyday actions: *choisir* (to choose), *réussir* (to succeed, to pass), *réfléchir* (to think it over), *remplir* (to fill, to fill out), *obéir* (to obey), *agir* (to act).
*Finir de* + infinitive = to finish doing: *Je finis de travailler à cinq heures.* *Choisir de* + infinitive = to choose to: *Il choisit de rester.*
*Réfléchir à* = to think about (consider): *Je réfléchis à ta question.* *Réussir* + noun = to pass: *Tu réussis ton examen.*
Negatives and questions work as usual: *Tu ne finis pas?* *Est-ce que vous choisissez?* *Finissez-vous tard?*

learn.h: Watch out: not every -ir verb follows finir
body: Some very common -ir verbs do NOT use *-iss-*: *dormir* (je dors, nous dormons), *partir*, *sortir*, *venir*, *ouvrir*. You will learn them next week.
If the verb is not on your -iss- list, check before you conjugate. The ones in this lesson are safe.
learn.tip: Nous dormons, but nous finissons: only the second group has -iss-.

body: In casual Quebec speech, *je* loses its vowel before these verbs: *j'finis*, *j'choisis* (the j even sounds like 'sh' before ch: [shwa-zi]).
*Il* and *ils* become *y*, and *elle* becomes *a*: *Y finit tard.* *Y choisissent toujours la même affaire.* *A réussit tout.* Recognise these; write the full forms.

examples.fr: Tu choisis le restaurant ce soir?
examples.en: Are you choosing the restaurant tonight?

examples.fr: Le film finit à dix heures.
Nous choisissons un cadeau pour Marie.
examples.en: We're choosing a gift for Marie.

examples.fr: Vous remplissez ce formulaire, s'il vous plaît.
On finit de manger et on part.
examples.en: We finish eating and we leave.

examples.fr: Ils ne finissent pas avant minuit.
Mon père vieillit, mais il est en forme.
examples.en: My father is getting older, but he's in good shape.

examples.fr: Je rougis quand je parle en public.
examples.en: I blush when I speak in public.

examples.fr: Est-ce que vous finissez tôt le vendredi?
examples.en: Do you finish early on Fridays?
I'm going to choose the soup.
examples.note: futur proche: the infinitive choisir after vais

quebec.intro: Finir and choisir are everyday verbs, so you hear them in their shortest spoken forms: j'finis, y finit, a choisit. The grammar is the same; only the pronouns shrink.

items.note: sounds like 'shwazi': the j turns into ch before ch
elle → a, informal; toutt with the final t

items.std: Ils choisissent toujours la même chose.
items.qc: Y choisissent toujours la même affaire.
items.en: They always choose the same thing.
items.note: ils → y; une affaire = a thing, very common in Quebec

drills.why: Third person singular ends in -t: il choisit.

drills.q: Which verb does NOT follow the finir pattern?
'Y finissent tard' is Quebec speech for…
drills.why: Y = il or ils in fast speech; finissent shows it's plural.

drills.a: Je finis de travailler à cinq heures.

a: Le film finit à dix heures.
Le film se termine à dix heures.

drills.why: Ne … pas around finissent; ne is often dropped in speech.

vocab.ex: Le chien obéit à son maître.

pron.tip: Same sound: fee-NEE. Final s and t are silent.
shwa-zee-SON; the single s between vowels is [z], double ss is [s].
Quebec speech: shwa-ZEE, the j merges with ch.

dialogue.fr: Bonsoir! Vous choisissez maintenant ou vous réfléchissez encore?
dialogue.en: Good evening! Are you choosing now or still thinking?

dialogue.fr: Ma femme choisit la soupe, s'il vous plaît.
dialogue.en: My wife is having the soup, please.

dialogue.fr: Euh... je réfléchis. Les poutines sont grosses?
dialogue.en: Um... I'm thinking. Are the poutines big?

dialogue.fr: Oui, très grosses! Beaucoup de clients ne finissent pas.
dialogue.en: Yes, very big! Lots of customers don't finish.

dialogue.fr: Parfait, je choisis la petite poutine.
dialogue.en: Perfect, I'll choose the small poutine.

dialogue.fr: Très bien. La cuisine finit à dix heures, alors pas de problème.
dialogue.en: Very good. The kitchen closes at ten, so no problem.

speak.prompt: Say what time you finish work or school each day of the week.
speak.model: Le lundi, je finis à cinq heures. Le vendredi, je finis plus tôt, à trois heures.

speak.prompt: You're at a restaurant. Say what you choose, and what your friend chooses.
speak.model: Je choisis la soupe et mon ami choisit le poulet.

speak.prompt: Say 'I finish at five' the standard way, then the casual Quebec way.
speak.model: Je finis à cinq heures. / J'finis à cinq heures.

write.prompt: Write 5 sentences about your week using at least four different -ir verbs (finir, choisir, réussir, réfléchir, remplir…).
write.model: Le lundi, je finis de travailler à six heures. Le soir, je choisis une recette et je cuisine. Mon fils réussit bien à l'école. Ma fille grandit vite. Le vendredi, nous choisissons un film ensemble.

quiz.why: nous finissons, vous finissez, ils finissent.
Final s and t are silent: both [fi-ni].
Je réfléchis à ta question = I'm thinking about your question.
finir de + infinitive = to finish doing something.

quiz.q: Which verb follows the finir pattern?
quiz.why: Grandir: nous grandissons. The others have no -iss-.
maigrir = lose weight; grossir = gain weight.
